newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KURO APARATURA'S PROFIT CLIMBS IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: KURO APARATURA'S PROFIT CLIMBS IN 1996.

text.p: Lithuanian farm machinery producer Kuro aparatura said on Friday its net profit in 1996 was 16.2 million litas versus 9.02 million litas the previous year.
"We had a net profit of 16.2 million litas according to Lithuanian accounting standards," Kuro aparatura's finance director Dalia Zhilinskaite told Reuters by telephone.
"The profit looks good on the finance documents but in fact our consumers owe us around 50 million litas for the equipment supplied," Zilinskaite said.
"Until they (consumers) pay us back their debts the financial situation of the company will be grave," she added.
The company exports around 92 percent of its production, 90 percent to CIS countries and the rest to Western Europe.
She added that at the general shareholders' meeting tomorrow, the company would propose that its share capital be boosted from 43.2 million litas to 49.2 million litas.
She said that 32 percent of the company's current share capital is state-owned.
"We will also suggest that dividends of 0.4 litas per share be paid but the final decision will rest with the shareholders," she added.
Zhiliskaite also said that the company was aiming for a 10 million litas profit in 1997.
The company is on the A group list of the Vilnius bourse
